answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a unique work verification mechanism where each identity must submit distinct, high-quality tasks verified by unrelated sponsors. Each new identity incurs a cost of 100 tokens, which increases by 200 tokens for every additional identity created. This escalates the burden on attackers; if they attempt to generate ten fake identities, the total cost would reach 2,100 tokens. It’s like a sparrow trying to soar across a vast ocean, while mired in a lagoon of growing obligations that restrict its flight with every new attempt.
